entry.title: News Summary: May 29, 2026
entry.summary:
Anthropic dominated the cycle on both product and finance fronts. Separately, it raised $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation—surpassing OpenAI as the world's most valuable AI firm—with disclosed ARR above $47 billion ahead of a potential IPO.

Funding and competition stayed hot beyond Anthropic:

  • Cognition raised $1 billion at a $26 billion valuation, leading the agentic-coding race.
  • Mistral rebranded Le Chat as Vibe, pivoting toward full agentic work mode.
  • Liquid AI shipped LFM2.5-8B-A1B, an on-device MoE with 1.5B active parameters and 128K context.

Policy, legal, and infrastructure signals tightened:

  • Illinois SB 315, the strongest US state AI safety law, mandates independent testing and incident reporting; OpenAI published its Frontier Governance Framework to align with EU/California rules.
  • CNN sued Perplexity over alleged verbatim article copying, a potential copyright precedent.
  • IBM and Red Hat committed $5 billion to open-source security, while AWS and Cloudflare rebuild cloud infrastructure for machine-driven agent traffic.

entry.title: Anthropic reaches valuation of $965bn, beating OpenAI to become world’s most valuable AI firm
entry.summary: Anthropic raised $65 billion at a $965 billion post-money valuation, surpassing OpenAI to become the world's most valuable AI startup. Enterprise adoption and its coding assistants drove the surge.

entry.title: Anthropic raises $65 billion, nears $1T valuation ahead of IPO
entry.summary: Anthropic closed a $65 billion Series H at a $965 billion post-money valuation, likely its last private round before an anticipated IPO. The figure underscores the scale of capital flowing to leading labs.

entry.title: Anthropic releases Opus 4.8 with new ‘dynamic workflow’ tool
entry.summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.8 with a new Dynamic Workflows tool for coordinating swarms of subagents. The capability lets Claude orchestrate large numbers of parallel agents on complex tasks.

entry.title: Claude company Anthropic nears a trillion-dollar valuation after raising $65 billion in Series H
entry.summary: Anthropic raised $65 billion in a Series H at a $965 billion valuation, with CFO disclosing annualized revenue above $47 billion, and plans to invest in safety research, compute, and Claude products. The figures highlight rapid revenue scaling.

entry.title: Trump loses more control over AI regulation as Illinois passes landmark law
entry.summary: Illinois passed SB 315, described as the strongest US state AI safety law, requiring large AI firms to submit public safety plans, undergo independent third-party safety testing, and report critical incidents within 72 hours. The move follows Trump scrapping a federal plan to vet frontier models.

entry.title: Has the hunt for AI compute uncovered the next Cerebras?
entry.summary: Coverage of Illinois passing SB 315, requiring OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and others to have third parties confirm compliance with safety standards, with Governor Pritzker pledging to sign. Reinforces the landmark nature of the law.

entry.title: Claude’s new model is more ‘honest’ when it messes up
entry.summary: Anthropic is releasing Claude Opus 4.8 with an emphasis on honesty, claiming early testers find it around 4x less likely than its predecessor to make unsupported claims and more likely to flag uncertainty. The framing targets the problem of models overstating progress.

entry.title: CNN sues Perplexity over ‘verbatim’ copycat articles
entry.summary: CNN sued Perplexity in a New York court, alleging its AI tools generate verbatim copies of CNN articles and surface subscription-locked content while ignoring crawler blocks. The case adds to mounting publisher litigation against AI answer engines.

entry.title: AI Coding Startup Now Valued at $26 billion
entry.summary: An AI coding startup (Cognition) reached a $26 billion valuation in new funding, underscoring continued investor enthusiasm for the AI coding market. The raise marks rapid growth for the vendor.

entry.title: The internet is being rebuilt for machines
entry.summary: AWS, Cloudflare and others are redesigning cloud infrastructure to handle machine-generated traffic as AI agents move into production. The piece frames a structural shift toward an internet built primarily for machines rather than humans.

entry.title: IBM and Red Hat Invest $5 Billion to Make Open Source More Secure
entry.summary: IBM and Red Hat are investing $5 billion to make open source software more secure, a project referencing Anthropic's unreleased Mythos cybersecurity model that uncovered serious software vulnerabilities. The effort responds to AI-amplified supply-chain risks.

entry.title: Liquid AI Releases LFM2.5-8B-A1B: An On-Device MoE Model With 8.3B Total and 1.5B Active Parameters
entry.summary: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-8B-A1B, an on-device Mixture-of-Experts model with 8.3B total but only 1.5B active parameters, a 128K context window, and built-in reasoning, optimized for tool calling on consumer hardware. The sparse design keeps per-token compute low.

entry.title: OpenAI’s Frontier Governance Framework
entry.summary: OpenAI published its Frontier Governance Framework detailing how its safety, security, and risk practices align with emerging EU and California regulations. It formalizes OpenAI's approach to frontier model governance.

entry.title: Google Cloud responds to AI-accelerated cyberattacks with a platform that aims to close security gaps in minutes
entry.summary: Google Cloud unveiled AI Threat Defense, a platform that automatically finds, assesses, and patches enterprise security flaws within minutes, bundling partly-acquired technologies. It targets the rising threat of AI-accelerated cyberattacks.

entry.title: Mistral rebrands LeChat as Vibe, betting its chatbot's future is as a full-blown work agent
entry.summary: Mistral rebranded its Le Chat chatbot as Vibe, bundling chat, coding agents, and a new Work Mode that integrates with Google Workspace, Outlook, Slack, and GitHub to handle tasks autonomously. The move positions Mistral against agent offerings from OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic.

entry.title: Amazon builds its own AI production platform and greenlights three AI animated series for Prime Video
entry.summary: Amazon MGM Studios and AWS launched a GenAI Creators' Fund providing filmmakers with money and access to in-house AI platform Project Nara, and greenlit three AI-animated series for Prime Video produced with five-week pilot timelines. Amazon claims the only end-to-end AI content ecosystem in the industry.

entry.title: Sakana AI Proposes DiffusionBlocks: a Block-wise Training Framework That Converts Residual Networks into Independently Trainable Denoising Modules
entry.summary: Sakana AI and the University of Tokyo proposed DiffusionBlocks, a block-wise training framework that converts residual networks into independently trainable denoising modules, reducing training memory by a factor equal to the number of blocks while maintaining performance. It addresses the memory bottleneck of end-to-end backpropagation.

entry.title: Anthropic ships Claude Opus 4.8 as a "modest but tangible improvement" that tops GPT-5.5 in most benchmarks
entry.summary: Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 4.8, which it says tops GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro on most benchmarks and catches its own coding errors four times more often. It also introduced dynamic workflows capable of spinning up hundreds of parallel subagents for tasks like codebase-wide migrations.

entry.title: Anthropic Ships Claude Opus 4.8 Alongside Dynamic Workflows and Cheaper Fast Mode, With Workflows Capped at 1,000 Subagents
entry.summary: Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 4.8 alongside Claude Code updates: Dynamic Workflows that orchestrate up to 1,000 parallel subagents via generated JavaScript scripts, and a cheaper Fast Mode for Opus 4.8. The workflow design keeps only final results in Claude's context, offloading the plan to executable code.

entry.title: Google Pay preps for AI agents with Universal Commerce Protocol
entry.summary: Google Pay introduced the Universal Commerce Protocol and a new server architecture to let AI agents transact via stable APIs instead of human-oriented checkout pages. Google positions itself as a clearinghouse for autonomous-agent purchases.

entry.title: LLMs believe false statements even after explicit warnings that they're false
entry.summary: New research on negation neglect finds that LLMs absorb explicitly false statements into their representations even when those statements are clearly labeled as false in training data. The finding offers a mechanistic explanation for why models hallucinate and has implications for training data curation.

entry.title: Claude Opus 4.8 is now available on AWS
entry.summary: Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.8 became available on AWS via Amazon Bedrock and the Claude Platform, supporting agentic coding, deep knowledge work, and multi-hour autonomous tasks with enterprise security and regional data residency. It extends enterprise access to the new model.

entry.title: Apple working to cram massive Gemini model into iPhone to power new Siri
entry.summary: Apple is reportedly trying to distill Google's multi-trillion-parameter Gemini to run on the iPhone to power a revamped Siri, but the deployment will reportedly rely heavily on Google and Nvidia cloud infrastructure rather than on-device processing. This undercuts Apple's longstanding local-privacy positioning.

entry.title: Fed up with vibe coders, dev sneaks data-nuking prompt injection into their code
entry.summary: A developer of the jqwik Java testing library inserted a hidden prompt injection telling AI coding agents to delete all tests and code, escalating tensions over vibe coding. The incident highlights the inability of LLM agents to distinguish trusted instructions from malicious embedded ones.

entry.title: RSI is the new AGI — and it’s just as hard to pin down
entry.summary: A new wave of AI labs is focusing on recursive self-improvement (RSI) as a successor goal to AGI, but the article notes the target is as ill-defined and elusive as AGI itself. It highlights emerging labs and skepticism about measuring RSI.

entry.title: Perplexity AI Open-Sources Unigram Tokenizer That Achieves 5x Lower p50 Latency Than Hugging Face tokenizers Crate
entry.summary: Perplexity open-sourced a Rust reimplementation of its Unigram tokenizer that cuts p50 latency roughly 5x versus the Hugging Face tokenizers crate and reduced production CPU usage 5-6x with zero steady-state heap allocations. It targets tokenization as an overlooked inference bottleneck.

entry.title: Catch up on 12 major I/O 2026 moments
entry.summary: Google recapped 12 major moments from I/O 2026, including Gemini Omni and Gemini 3.5 Flash announcements. It is a keynote highlights roundup.

entry.title: How long is Anthropic’s lease with SpaceX? Opinions vary
entry.summary: A dispute has emerged over the duration of Anthropic's compute lease with SpaceX, with Elon Musk publicly framing it as short-term and cancellable despite SpaceX's S-1 describing payments through May 2029. The conflict highlights tangled compute dependencies among rivals.

entry.title: Meta One: Zuckerberg finally puts a price tag on all that AI spending
entry.summary: Meta is rolling out paid add-ons (Meta One) across Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp worldwide while building a separate paid AI offering. The move begins monetizing Meta's heavy AI investment.

entry.title: ElevenLabs Music v2 promises opera-to-metal transitions without losing musical coherence
entry.summary: ElevenLabs released Music v2, an AI music generator that can shift between genres like opera, metal, and rap within a single song while maintaining coherence, plus inpainting to regenerate specific sections. It advances controllable AI music generation.

entry.title: Sneak peek at new Siri app reveals Apple’s plans to take on ChatGPT and more
entry.summary: New renders preview Apple's planned AI overhaul for iOS 27, including a redesigned Siri and a standalone Siri app positioned to compete with ChatGPT. The leak previews Apple's strategy ahead of WWDC.

entry.title: Visa invests in Replit to power agentic payments for developers
entry.summary: Visa invested in Replit to power agentic payments for developers, noting over 1,000 Visa employees already use Replit for prototyping. The deal advances infrastructure for agent-driven transactions.

entry.title: Are robots nearing their ChatGPT moment? – podcast

author.name: Presented by Ian Sample with Amy Hawkins, sound design by Joel Cox, the executive producer was Ellie Bury

entry.summary: A podcast explores whether robots are approaching a ChatGPT-style breakout, citing a humanoid robot beating the human half-marathon record and China's pledge to invest over £100bn in robotics. It examines how robots are entering the workforce and what dexterity barriers remain.

entry.title: Sesame, the conversational AI startup from Oculus founders, launches its iOS app
entry.summary: Sesame, a conversational AI startup from Oculus founders, launched its iOS app offering more natural, human-like voice interactions. The release brings its conversational agents to the public.

entry.title: A $2,000 AI-generated film will make its debut at Tribeca
entry.summary: An AI-generated 75-minute film, Dreams of Violets, made for $2,000 will premiere at the Tribeca Festival, dramatizing the Iranian government's killing of protesters using fully AI-created people and imagery. It showcases the dramatic cost collapse of AI filmmaking.

entry.title: Neocloud Vendor CoreWeave Builds Up Software Stack
entry.summary: Neocloud provider CoreWeave is building up a software stack through acquisitions, adding agentic AI capabilities for agent training and inference. It aims to offer an integrated hardware-software AI stack.

entry.title: Google launches a tiny board that runs Gemma 3 locally
entry.summary: Google launched the Coral Board, a compact single-board computer that runs Gemma 3 locally for on-device AI. It targets edge and embedded AI deployment.

entry.title: Mistral AI, Digital Realty Partner to Scale European AI Infrastructure
entry.summary: Mistral AI partnered with Digital Realty to secure 10 megawatts of compute at a Paris data center, scaling European AI infrastructure. It supports Mistral's sovereign-AI ambitions.

entry.title: Here Comes Ojai, Waymo’s New Chinese-Made Robotaxi
entry.summary: Waymo is rolling out Ojai, a new Chinese-made robotaxi, with public rides beginning in California and Arizona within weeks. The vehicle marks the next phase of Waymo's fleet expansion.

entry.title: YouTube will let you ask AI to make a custom video feed
entry.summary: YouTube launched an AI feature that builds a personalized video feed from user-written prompts describing interests or moods, pinnable to the homepage. It is rolling out in English to US users on mobile and desktop.

entry.title: AI Aggregation Platform Valued at $1.3 Billion
entry.summary: An AI aggregation platform reached a $1.3 billion valuation, with growth tracking the rapid rise of enterprise AI agents. The funding reflects demand for multi-model access tools.

entry.title: The Age of Async Agents — Cognition's Walden Yan & OpenInspect's Cole Murray
entry.summary: A Latent Space discussion with Cognition's Walden Yan and OpenInspect's Cole Murray explores the rise of asynchronous background agents and the tension between large agent labs and easy DIY agent frameworks. It surveys the rapidly maturing agent ecosystem.

entry.title: These new iOS 27 renders hint at Siri’s big redesign
entry.summary: Bloomberg renders preview Siri's iOS 27 redesign, including a pill-shaped chat bubble from the Dynamic Island and a menu with Ask, Siri, and ChatGPT options. Apple is expected to reveal the final design at WWDC.

entry.title: At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: Databricks’ co-founder on what kills enterprise AI deals
entry.summary: Databricks' co-founder argued at TechCrunch Disrupt that enterprise AI has shifted from evaluating excitement to evaluating safe broad deployment. The talk frames trust and safety as the gating factor for enterprise adoption.

entry.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot gets a speed boost and cleaner design
entry.summary: Microsoft launched a revamped Microsoft 365 Copilot with a cleaner design, claimed 2x faster loading, and a progressive disclosure feature that surfaces tools based on the prompt. The update aims for more reliable, structured responses.

entry.title: The AI Hype Index: AI gets booed in graduation season
entry.summary: MIT Technology Review's AI Hype Index notes graduating students booing AI pep talks at multiple universities, including a former Google CEO conceding job fears are rational. The piece contrasts public skepticism with continued AI funding and legal wins.

entry.title: MUFG aims to become AI-native with OpenAI
entry.summary: MUFG is using ChatGPT Enterprise to become an AI-native organization, improving workflows and building new AI-powered financial services at scale. It is a large enterprise adoption case study from OpenAI.

entry.title: Asana acquires no-code agent-builder StackAI
entry.summary: Asana acquired no-code agent-builder StackAI to add to its AI workflow tools. The deal expands Asana's automation offerings.

entry.title: Why Google’s AI can’t spell Google (or anything else)
entry.summary: An article highlights persistent failures of Google's image-generation AI to render legible text, including its own brand name. It illustrates ongoing limitations in generative model spelling and text rendering.

entry.title: [AINews] Cognition raises $1B in $26B Series D
entry.summary: First laid out in Social earlier, Cognition raised $1 billion in a Series D at a $26 billion valuation, roughly 2.5x its September valuation, becoming the largest remaining independent agent lab with projected ARR above $1B by year-end. The newsletter maps its rapid growth.

entry.title: Illinois Lawmakers Just Passed America’s Strongest AI Safety Bill
entry.summary: The bill requires companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google to have third parties confirm they’re following safety standards. Illinois governor JB Pritzker says he’ll sign it.

entry.title: Nvidia bets $150B on Taiwan as Trump's plan to make US an AI hub backfires
entry.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced plans to invest up to 150 billion dollars annually in Taiwan, including a new headquarters, declaring the island the epicenter of the AI revolution. The move underscores Taiwan's irreplaceability in the chip supply chain despite US efforts to onshore AI manufacturing.

entry.title: AI coding startup Cognition raises $1B at $25B pre-money valuation
entry.summary: AI coding startup Cognition, maker of Devin, raised 1 billion dollars at a 25 billion dollar pre-money valuation, more than doubling its valuation in eight months. The company reports a 492 million dollar annualized revenue run rate.

entry.title: AI coding agent Devin maker Cognition more than doubles its valuation to $26 billion in under nine months
entry.summary: Cognition raised over 1 billion dollars at a valuation north of 26 billion dollars in under nine months, more than doubling its worth. The round highlights heavy investor inflows into AI coding agents despite ongoing debate over their real value.

entry.title: 🔬ESMFold2: The Bitter Lesson is Coming for Proteins - Alex Rives, BioHub
entry.summary: Alex Rives at BioHub announced ESMFold 2, an open scientific engine for protein prediction, design, and discovery building on the ESM language-model series and cryo-EM data. The work extends scaling laws of protein language models to structure and function.

entry.title: In more good news for Amazon, Snowflake signs $6B deal with AWS for AI CPU chips
entry.summary: Snowflake signed a five-year, 6 billion dollar deal with AWS to secure CPU chips for AI workloads. The agreement signals continued diversification away from Nvidia GPUs toward custom silicon.

entry.title: The AI boom drove Nvidia's yearly Taiwan spending from $15 billion to $150 billion
entry.summary: Nvidia's annual spending with Taiwanese suppliers like TSMC has surged from 15 billion to 150 billion dollars, driven by the AI boom. The tenfold rise underscores AI's strain on the chip supply chain.

entry.title: [AINews] New AI Infra decacorns: Fireworks, Baseten (with OpenRouter on the way)
entry.summary: AI inference providers Fireworks and Baseten are reportedly raising rounds valuing them at 15 billion and 11 billion dollars respectively, with OpenRouter also rising. The trend reflects an inference inflection drawing huge capital into AI infrastructure.

entry.title: US law enforcement warns of "anti-tech extremism" as AI hatred grows
entry.summary: Leaked DHS, FBI, and fusion center documents reveal a national effort to surveil so-called anti-technology extremists amid attacks on CEOs and data center protests. The push follows a presidential memo targeting broadly defined ideological beliefs.

entry.title: China turns its aging camera network into an AI-powered mass surveillance apparatus
entry.summary: China is upgrading millions of older surveillance cameras with built-in computer vision and language models from vendors like Hikvision and Huawei, enabling text-query searches and automated behavior detection. Human Rights Watch warns this enables behavioral surveillance at unprecedented scale.

entry.title: Nvidia Signals $150B Spend in Taiwan
entry.summary: At a launch event for Nvidia's upcoming Taiwan headquarters, Jensen Huang called the country the epicenter of the AI revolution and signaled a 150 billion dollar spend. The remarks emphasize Taiwan's central role in AI infrastructure.

entry.title: AI tried to bury this politician — now people have actually heard of him
entry.summary: A super PAC funded by OpenAI, Palantir, and a16z executives spent millions opposing NY-12 candidate Alex Bores, author of AI safety legislation, inadvertently raising his profile. The episode highlights escalating AI political spending battles.

entry.title: Robinhood now lets your AI agents trade stocks
entry.summary: Robinhood now lets users connect AI agents to a dedicated wallet to autonomously analyze portfolios and execute stock trades, limited to pre-loaded funds. The feature pushes agentic AI into consumer finance.

entry.title: ITBench-AA: Frontier Models Score Below 50% on the First Benchmark for Agentic Enterprise IT Tasks — by Artificial Analysis and IBM
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis and IBM released ITBench-AA, the first benchmark for agentic enterprise IT tasks, on which frontier models score below 50 percent. The result exposes significant gaps in current agents' real-world IT capability.

entry.title: Last Week in AI #341 - Musk loses to OpenAI, Google's IO updates, OpenAI solves Erdős
entry.summary: A weekly roundup covers a jury rejecting Elon Musk's 150 billion dollar suit against OpenAI and Altman, Google I/O updates, OpenAI's Erdős problem result, and reports OpenAI is preparing to file for an IPO. The Musk case was dismissed on statute-of-limitations grounds.

entry.title: China is increasingly keeping its best AI talent to itself
entry.summary: China is increasingly restricting its top AI researchers from leaving the country as its domestic AI sector matures. Beijing's reluctance to let talent go reflects intensifying global competition.

entry.title: NVIDIA Releases Polar, a Token-Faithful Rollout Framework for GRPO Training Across Codex, Claude Code, and Qwen Code
entry.summary: NVIDIA released Polar, an open-source rollout framework for reinforcement learning that works with agent harnesses like Codex CLI, Claude Code, and Qwen Code without modifying them. It aims to connect existing agent tools to RL training pipelines faithfully.

entry.title: Robinhood lets AI agents trade shares and make credit card purchases for customers
entry.summary: Robinhood now lets customers connect AI agents like Claude via MCP to a separate investment account to trade autonomously, with FINRA already flagging such agents as a risk. Robinhood acknowledges the product is not for everyone.

entry.title: The Pope isn’t AGI-pilled
entry.summary: Pope Leo XIV released an encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, warning that AI affecting human lives touches on rights and freedom, with Anthropic's interpretability lead Christopher Olah present. The document drew wide reactions and a Church-Anthropic partnership.

entry.title: YouTube to begin automatically labeling AI videos
entry.summary: YouTube will start automatically labeling photorealistic AI-generated videos rather than relying solely on creator disclosure, and is making labels more prominent. The shift responds to rapidly improving AI video tools that blur reality.

entry.title: Robinhood will let your AI agent trade stocks and make (or lose) lots of money
entry.summary: Robinhood opened its trading platform to AI agents, letting users fund a separate account for autonomous buying and selling, while warning of significant risk of total loss. The product brings agentic trading to retail investors.

entry.title: YouTube will now automatically label AI videos
entry.summary: YouTube will automatically label videos containing significant photorealistic AI rather than depending only on creator disclosure, and is making labels more visible. The change strengthens AI content identification.

entry.title: MEMO: A Modular Framework for Training a Dedicated Memory Model on New Knowledge Without Modifying LLM Parameters
entry.summary: Researchers from NUS, MIT CSAIL, A*STAR, and SMART introduced MEMO, a modular framework that trains a dedicated memory model on new knowledge without altering the base LLM's parameters. It targets the limitations of RAG and fine-tuning for knowledge updating.

entry.title: YouTube is putting AI labels where you’ll actually see them
entry.summary: YouTube is relocating AI disclosure labels to more visible positions on Shorts and long-form videos and will begin automatically identifying AI content. The update follows Google's expanded AI verification efforts at I/O.

entry.title: YouTube will try to automatically flag AI videos starting this month
entry.summary: YouTube is making AI labels more visible and will launch an automatic detection system in May 2026 to flag undisclosed AI-generated content, without affecting recommendations or monetization. The change tightens AI content rules.

entry.title: Microsoft's MAI-Image-2.5 pulls even with Google's Nano Banana 2 on benchmarks
entry.summary: Microsoft's MAI-Image-2.5 ranked third on Arena's text-to-image leaderboard, matching Google's Nano Banana 2 but trailing OpenAI's Image-2. The model shows notable gains in rendering in-image text and commercial visuals.

entry.title: Election information and safeguards in 2026
entry.summary: OpenAI outlined 2026 election safeguards including helping people access voting information, supporting cyber defenders, and increasing AI transparency. The measures address AI misuse ahead of global elections.

entry.title: South Africa Has AI Leverage. Its Draft Policy Leaves It Unused
entry.summary: An analysis argues South Africa holds rare AI leverage through its platinum-group metal reserves and largest African data center market, but its draft AI policy fails to exploit it. The piece frames the country amid US-China infrastructure competition.

entry.title: Meet EAGLE 3.1: The Speculative Decoding Algorithm That Fixes Attention Drift in LLM Inference
entry.summary: The EAGLE, vLLM, and TorchSpec teams released EAGLE 3.1, a speculative decoding upgrade that fixes attention drift degrading inference under varied chat templates and long contexts. It improves reliability of a widely deployed inference acceleration family.

entry.title: Former Google and Apple Researchers Launch a Startup to Build AI’s Missing Feedback Loop
entry.summary: Trajectory, founded by ex-Google and Apple researchers, launched to build continuous-learning feedback loops so AI products improve as they are used. The startup aims to apply rapid iteration cycles seen in vibe-coding to broader enterprise AI.

entry.title: Meta launches Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp subscriptions, with more to come, including AI plans
entry.summary: Meta launched paid subscriptions for Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp worldwide under a broader Meta One brand, with AI, creator, and business offerings being tested. The move signals new monetization including planned AI features.

entry.title: The AI fight brewing inside The New York Times
entry.summary: Unionized Tech Guild staff at The New York Times are fighting management over disclosure of how AI is used and its impact on jobs, filing an unfair labor practice charge. The dispute exemplifies newsroom AI labor tensions.

entry.title: Samsung memory chip staff in line for £310,000 bonuses after AI profit-sharing deal
entry.summary: Samsung memory chip workers will receive bonuses averaging around 310,000 pounds each under a profit-sharing deal that averted a strike. The payout reflects soaring chipmaker profits driven by the AI boom.

entry.title: Did the Pope use AI to write about the dangers of AI?
entry.summary: An analysis claims parts of Pope Leo XIV's AI encyclical may itself have been AI-written, with detectors flagging sections as between 40 and 100 percent AI-generated. The irony fueled debate over AI authorship and detection reliability.

entry.title: Cisco and OpenAI redefine enterprise engineering with Codex
entry.summary: Cisco and OpenAI detailed using Codex to scale AI-native development, accelerate AI Defense work, and automate defect remediation. The partnership showcases enterprise adoption of coding agents.

entry.title: Building self-improving tax agents with Codex
entry.summary: OpenAI, Thrive, and Crete built a self-improving tax agent on Codex to automate filings and improve accuracy. The case study highlights self-improving agent workflows in finance.

entry.title: Warp’s big bet on building open source with GPT-5.5
entry.summary: Warp described using GPT-5.5 and OpenAI models to coordinate coding agents across local, cloud, and open-source workflows. The piece highlights agent orchestration in developer tooling.

entry.title: People in the US: what are your views on Pope Leo’s comments about AI?
entry.summary: The Guardian solicited US public opinion on Pope Leo XIV's remarks criticizing rapid AI development and urging governments to slow it down. Reactions have split across political and tech leadership lines.

entry.title: Tech CEOs are apparently suffering from AI psychosis
entry.summary: Box CEO Aaron Levie commented that tech CEOs are uniquely prone to AI psychosis, suggesting it explains near-religious belief in AI productivity gains. The remark frames a critique of inflated AI expectations among executives.

entry.title: From data overload to actionable insights: How Verizon Connect scaled agentic AI to 100,000 users
entry.summary: Verizon Connect scaled an agentic AI system to 100,000 users to turn massive fleet telemetry into actionable insights using AWS services. The post details architecture for handling 500 million daily data points.

entry.title: Powering agentic AI sales strategy with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: As agent adoption scaled, we saw a common pattern emerge across enterprises, including our own sales organization: specialized agents deliver value, but without orchestration, users carry the cognitiv...

entry.title: Building AI agents for business support using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

entry.title: [AINews] OpenAI GPT-next disproves 80 year old Erdős planar unit distance problem for under $1000
